title: “One who avoids sensual desires As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head — That mindful one transcends This attachment in the world. Whoever is greedy…
content:
“One who avoids sensual desires
As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one transcends
This attachment in the world.

Whoever is greedy for sensual pleasures —
Land, gold, cows, horses,
Servants, attendants, women, relatives —

Weak, overcome by sensual pleasures,
Calamity crushes him,
Suffering follows him
As water rushes into a broken boat.

Therefore, always mindful,
One should abandon sensual pleasures.
Having abandoned them, one crosses the flood,
Having bailed out the boat, one reaches the far shore.”

title: “Monks, how is it that Māra and his followers cannot reach? Here, monks, a monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states,…
content: “Monks, how is it that Māra and his followers cannot reach? Here, monks, a monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This, monks, is called a monk who has blinded Māra, obliterated Māra’s track, leaving no trace, making Māra unable to find his path. Furthermore, monks, a monk, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, without initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration. This is called a monk who has blinded Māra, obliterated Māra’s track, leaving no trace, making Māra unable to find his path.”

title: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The…
content: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world. These five perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless.”

title: “Monks, when form is born, subsists, arises, and becomes manifest — that is the birth of suffering, the subsisting of disease, the manifestation of aging…
content: “Monks, when form is born, subsists, arises, and becomes manifest — that is the birth of suffering, the subsisting of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. When feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is born, subsists, arises, and becomes manifest — that is the birth of suffering, the subsisting of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. When form ceases, subsides, and passes away — that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of disease, the passing away of aging and death. When feeling … perception … formations … consciousness ceases, subsides, and passes away — that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of disease, the passing away of aging and death.”

title: “Here, these evil, unwholesome intentions of sensual desire, ill-will, and agitation are a hindrance for the noble disciple in training. Here, monks, a noble disciple…
content: “Here, these evil, unwholesome intentions of sensual desire, ill-will, and agitation are a hindrance for the noble disciple in training. Here, monks, a noble disciple reflects: ‘Sensual pleasures present and future, perceptions of sensual pleasure present and future — both belong to Māra’s realm, Māra’s domain, Māra’s bait, Māra’s food. Suppose I dwell with a mind that is expansive, great, having conquered the world and established the mind’s position. When I dwell with a mind that is expansive, great, having conquered the world and established the mind’s position, then those evil, unwholesome intentions of sensual desire, ill-will, and agitation will not arise; with their abandonment, my mind does not become confined, but rather immeasurable and well-developed.’”

title: “And what, monks, is the cessation of suffering? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact…
content: “And what, monks, is the cessation of suffering? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. With feeling as condition, craving. But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving, clinging ceases. With the cessation of clinging, existence ceases. With the cessation of existence, birth ceases. With the cessation of birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering. This is the cessation of suffering. Dependent on the ear … on the nose … on the tongue … on the body … Dependent on the mind and phenomena, mind-consciousness arises … With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering. This is the cessation of suffering.”

title: Then the Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthi, mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by…
content:
Then the Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthi, mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by sensual pleasures. Then the Blessed One, understanding the meaning, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

Blinded by sensual pleasures,
Covered by a net,
Veiled by craving,
Bound by the fetter of heedlessness —
Like fish caught in a net,
They go to aging and death,
Like a suckling calf to its mother.

title: - What is called the wrong path? What destroys day and night? What defiles the holy life? What is a bath without water? - Greed…
content:
- What is called the wrong path?
What destroys day and night?
What defiles the holy life?
What is a bath without water?
- Greed is called the wrong path,
Aging destroys day and night,
Women defile the holy life,
Ensnaring humankind —
Austerities and the holy life
Are a bath without water.

title: Then the female demon Arati (Discontent) recited this verse to the Blessed One: How does a monk, Living amidst many obstacles, Having crossed the five…
content:
Then the female demon Arati (Discontent) recited this verse to the Blessed One:
How does a monk,
Living amidst many obstacles,
Having crossed the five floods,
Strive to cross the sixth?
How can he meditate,
Amidst many sensual perceptions,
So that they remain outside him,
Not catching him?

(The Blessed One):
With body tranquilized,
With mind well liberated,
With no more activities,
Mindful, without clinging,
Knowing the Dhamma,
Without thought, meditating —
Without anger, without distraction,
Without drowsiness, without laziness —
Thus the monk,
Living amidst many obstacles,
Having crossed the five floods,
Strives to cross the sixth.
Thus he meditates,
Amidst many sensual perceptions,
They remain outside him,
Not catching him.

title: “Monks, these nine perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, having the deathless as their end. What…
content: “Monks, these nine perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, having the deathless as their end. What nine? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion. These nine perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, having the deathless as their end.”
